extracted.intended_audience: media members, publishers, editors, journalists and VOD service providers who are members of (or subject to) the NZ Media Council
extracted.subtask_short: NZ Media Council principles and VOD code
extracted.subtask_description: Statement of Principles governing print/online editorial conduct plus a Video-on-Demand (VOD) Classifications Code for NZ Media Council members, setting ethical standards and VOD classification, display and complaints rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, Fairness and Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications should be bound at all times by accuracy, fairness and balance and should not deliberately mislead or misinform readers by commission or omission. In articles of controversy or disagreement, a fair voice must be given to the opposition view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may apply for long-running issues where every side cannot reasonably be repeated on every occasion and in reportage of proceedings where balance is to be judged over a number of stories rather than a single report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone is normally entitled to privacy of person, space and personal information and these rights should be respected by publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right of privacy should not interfere with publication of significant matters of public record or public interest. Publishers should exercise care before identifying relatives of persons convicted or accused of crime where reference is not relevant. Those suffering trauma or grief call for special consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children and Young People
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases involving children and young people publishers must demonstrate an exceptional degree of public interest to override the interests of the child or young person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment and Fact
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear distinction should be drawn between factual information and comment or opinion. A publication that is essentially comment or opinion should be clearly presented as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance is not required in comment or opinion publications, although material facts on which an opinion is based should be accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Columns, Blogs, Opinion and Letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters and online comments for publication are the prerogative of editors who are to be guided by fairness, balance and public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abridgement is acceptable but should not distort meaning. Letters, online comments and cartoons are understood to be opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines and Captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines, sub-headings, and captions should accurately and fairly convey the substance or a key element of the report they are designed to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination and Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues of gender, religion, minority groups, sexual orientation, age, race, colour or physical or mental disability are legitimate subjects for discussion where relevant and in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should not place gratuitous emphasis on any such category in their reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications have a strong obligation to protect against disclosure of the identity of confidential sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers must take reasonable steps to satisfy themselves that confidential sources are well informed and reliable. Care should be taken to ensure source and journalist agree on what is meant by 'off-the-record'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subterfuge
rubrics_metrics.description: Information or news obtained by subterfuge, misrepresentation or dishonest means is not permitted unless there is an overriding public interest and the news cannot be obtained by any other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and publishers must be independent and free of obligations to their news sources and should avoid situations that might compromise such independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a story is enabled by sponsorship, gift or financial inducement, that sponsorship/gift/inducement should be declared and labelled. Where an author’s link to a subject is justified, the relationship should be declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and Graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should take care in the creation, selection and treatment of photographs and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any technical manipulation that could mislead readers should be noted and explained. Photographs showing distressing or shocking situations should be handled with special consideration for those affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: A publisher’s willingness to correct errors enhances credibility and will often defuse the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant errors should be promptly corrected with fair prominence. In some circumstances it will be appropriate to offer an apology and a right of reply to affected persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of VOD Classifications Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Require media members to classify their video-on-demand programmes in a socially responsible way that enables parents to protect children and make informed viewing choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifications must be appropriately displayed at the point when viewing choices are being made; the Code balances freedom of expression and sufficient information for viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: Definition of VOD programmes and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: VOD programmes means a film or entertainment programme delivered after the viewer selects it from a member’s VOD service and includes promotions for the member's own programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes sports programmes, live or 'as-live' programmes, user-generated content not under editorial control of a Member, and news and current affairs programmes (which are subject to the Council’s Statement of Principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Members must classify VOD programmes in accordance with the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must classify VOD programmes in accordance with this Code or an alternative set of classifications and visual warning symbols approved by the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may apply alternative classifications only if the Council has determined those alternatives are consistent with the Code's objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification categories and meanings (G, PG, M, 16, 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code's classifications are: G (approved for general viewing), PG (parental guidance recommended), M (suitable for mature audiences 16+), 16 (people under 16 should not view), 18 (people under 18 should not view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G: exclude material likely unsuitable for children. PG: may be suitable for children with parental guidance; parents expected to monitor. M: contains adult themes directed at mature audiences — check descriptive note. 16: contains stronger material outside M (examples: greater sexual activity, potentially offensive language, realistic violence, sexual violence, horrific encounters). 18: contains themes which may be challenging or offensive even to some adult viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of additional visual warning symbols (C, L, V, S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where programme content is likely to offend or disturb a significant number of the intended audience, additional visual warning symbols must be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols: C (content may offend), L (language may offend), V (violence may offend), S (sexual material may offend).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply equivalent classifications where previously rated
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a VOD programme has already been rated or classified in New Zealand or elsewhere, the member may apply the equivalent classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified under NZ Code of Broadcasting Standards or by Film and Video Labelling Body of NZ use the equivalent. Where rated acceptable for under-16 in another country, member may apply equivalent G, PG or M under this Code. See Council list of accepted overseas classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification assessment by trained staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification assessment under this Code should be carried out by trained staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of classifications with programme listings
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification must be clearly displayed with the VOD programme listing information on a member's VOD website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must provide information for viewers about the meaning of classifications and visual warning symbols; this information must be easily accessible to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage child-protection measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are encouraged to consider measures to restrict child viewers from viewing adult material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints process: complain to member first, then Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone unhappy with a member’s classification of a VOD programme must complain to the media member in the first instance; if dissatisfied they may complain to the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council is independent and considers complaints under this Code. Members are bound by Council decisions. Complaints about breaches of privacy may be made to the Privacy Commissioner; complaints about online news/editorial content not covered by this Code can be made under the Council’s other jurisdictional mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and compliance with Council directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must comply with any direction from the Council to reclassify any VOD programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where content is reclassified, members must take all reasonable steps to have the content reclassified on any third-party sites they control and are aware the content has been published. If the Council upholds a complaint the decision will be published on the Council website. In egregious circumstances (unanimous decision) the Council may censure a member to the extent permitted under its rules and procedures. Other members publishing the same content must also comply when notified or otherwise aware.
